claims: 'Researchers found models get up to 39% dumber the longer a conversation goes' (terms: semantic degradation / context rot)

Creator intro: Stanford founder, AI startup, raised $4 million
how_to_steps: Open a new chat in Claude or ChatGPT and paste the skill-creation prompt (full text below)
When a conversation degrades, type /contexttransfer in that thread
Copy the single text block it returns into a fresh chat and continue
on_screen_only: Full prompt: 'Create the following skill and call it "Context Transfer". You're an expert at context summary. Your sole job is to package all key information from a conversation thread, so that I can use it in a new thread and continue the conversation without missing anything. Create a single text block with the following: 1. Our goals, task, key decisions & reasoning 2. Progress update: what's finished, in progress, not started 3. Every important file, link, name, figure, or detail 4. Where we left off & next steps 5. Any other key details - be granular as needed. Your response must be a single text block I can copy & paste into the new chat. The new chat must be able to seamlessly continue the conversation with no prior context other than your text block.'
Title card 'AI gets dumber the longer you chat'
Model selector reads 'Opus 5.3 Medium'; tabs 'Chat' / 'Cowork'; overlay '/contexttransfer'

relevance.why: Context rot is a daily problem for a founder running long Claude sessions; the prompt is complete and reusable. In Claude Code the native /compact and handoff files already cover this, but the structure is a good handoff template.

implement_score.why: Five minutes: save the prompt as a skill (claude.ai) or as a /handoff command in Claude Code that writes the five sections to a markdown file; aligns with the existing session-handoff practice.
